        "originalContents": "\n    const skilled = skilledSnap.docs\n      .map(doc =\u003e ({ ...doc.data(), uid: doc.id }))\n      .filter((crew: any) =\u003e crew.jobTitles \u0026\u0026 crew.jobTitles.some((job: any) =\u003e \n        ['Cinematography', 'Directing', 'Producing', 'Screenwriting', 'VFX', 'Sound Design'].some(skill =\u003e \n          job.title?.includes(skill) || job.department?.includes(skill)\n        )\n      )) as CrewProfile[];\n\n    // Merge all categories and deduplicate\n    const allCrew = [...newest, ...popular, ...available, ...experienced, ...skilled];\n    const uniqueCrew = deduplicate(allCrew, 'uid');\n\n    // Sort by a combination of factors: availability, project count, and recency\n    return uniqueCrew\n      .sort((a, b) =\u003e {\n        const aScore = (a.availability === 'available' ? 50 : 0) + \n                      ((a.projects?.length || 0) * 10) + \n                      (a.jobTitles?.length || 0);\n        const bScore = (b.availability === 'available' ? 50 : 0) + \n                      ((b.projects?.length || 0) * 10) + \n                      (b.jobTitles?.length || 0);\n        return bScore - aScore;\n      })\n      .slice(0, 8); // Return top 8 most engaging crew members\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Error fetching highlighted crew:', error);\n    return [];\n  }\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n\nexport class SocialService {\n  // Cache for frequently accessed data with separate timestamp tracking\n  private static profileCache = new Map\u003cstring, { profile: Profile; cachedAt: number }\u003e();\n  private static readonly CACHE_TTL = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes\n\n  /**\n   * Get a list of crew profiles (paginated)\n   */\n  static async getCrewProfiles(limitCount: number = 20, lastDocId?: string): Promise\u003cCrewProfile[]\u003e {\n    try {\n      let q = query(\n        collection(db, 'crewProfiles'),\n        orderBy('name'),\n        limit(limitCount)\n      );\n\n      // Add cursor for pagination if provided\n      if (lastDocId) {\n        const lastDoc = await getDoc(doc(db, 'crewProfiles', lastDocId));\n        if (lastDoc.exists()) {\n          q = query(q, where('name', '\u003e', lastDoc.data().name));\n        }\n      }\n\n      const querySnapshot = await getDocs(q);\n      return querySnapshot.docs.map(doc =\u003e {\n        const data = doc.data();\n        return {\n          id: doc.id,\n          uid: data.uid || doc.id,\n          name: data.name || '',\n          username: data.username || '',\n          bio: data.bio,\n          profileImageUrl: data.profileImageUrl,\n          jobTitles: data.jobTitles || [],\n          residences: data.residences || [],\n          projects: data.projects || [],\n          education: data.education || [],\n          contactInfo: data.contactInfo,\n          otherInfo: data.otherInfo,\n          isPublished: Boolean(data.isPublished),\n          availability: data.availability,\n          languages: data.languages || [],\n          createdAt: data.createdAt?.toDate(),\n          updatedAt: data.updatedAt?.toDate(),\n        } as CrewProfile;\n      });\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Error getting crew profiles:', error);\n      return [];\n    }\n  }",

        "originalContents": "\n\nexport class SocialService {\n  // Cache for frequently accessed data with separate timestamp tracking\n  private static profileCache = new Map\u003cstring, { profile: Profile; cachedAt: number }\u003e();\n  private static readonly CACHE_TTL = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes\n\n  /**\n   * Get a list of crew profiles (paginated)\n   */\n  static async getCrewProfiles(limitCount: number = 20, lastDocId?: string): Promise\u003cCrewProfile[]\u003e {\n    try {\n      let q = query(\n        collection(db, 'crewProfiles'),\n        orderBy('name'),\n        limit(limitCount)\n      );\n\n      // Add cursor for pagination if provided\n      if (lastDocId) {\n        const lastDoc = await getDoc(doc(db, 'crewProfiles', lastDocId));\n        if (lastDoc.exists()) {\n          q = query(q, where('name', '\u003e', lastDoc.data().name));\n        }\n      }\n\n      const querySnapshot = await getDocs(q);\n      return querySnapshot.docs.map(doc =\u003e {\n        const data = doc.data();\n        return {\n          id: doc.id,\n          uid: data.uid || doc.id,\n          name: data.name || '',\n          username: data.username || '',\n          bio: data.bio,\n          profileImageUrl: data.profileImageUrl,\n          jobTitles: data.jobTitles || [],\n          residences: data.residences || [],\n          projects: data.projects || [],\n          education: data.education || [],\n          contactInfo: data.contactInfo,\n          otherInfo: data.otherInfo,\n          isPublished: Boolean(data.isPublished),\n          availability: data.availability,\n          languages: data.languages || [],\n          createdAt: data.createdAt?.toDate(),\n          updatedAt: data.updatedAt?.toDate(),\n        } as CrewProfile;\n      });\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Error getting crew profiles:', error);\n      return [];\n    }\n  }",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n\n// Fetch highlighted crew: newest, most followed, and featured professionals\nexport async function getHighlightedCrew(): Promise\u003cCrewProfile[]\u003e {\n  const crewRef = collection(db, 'crewProfiles');\n\n  try {\n    // Get newest published profiles\n    const newestQ = query(crewRef, where('isPublished', '==', true), orderBy('createdAt', 'desc'), limit(4));\n    const newestSnap = await getDocs(newestQ);\n    const newest = newestSnap.docs.map(doc =\u003e ({ ...doc.data(), uid: doc.id })) as CrewProfile[];\n\n    // Get most followed profiles\n    const popularQ = query(crewRef, where('isPublished', '==', true), orderBy('followersCount', 'desc'), limit(4));\n    const popularSnap = await getDocs(popularQ);\n    const popular = popularSnap.docs.map(doc =\u003e ({ ...doc.data(), uid: doc.id })) as CrewProfile[];\n\n    // Get available crew members\n    const availableQ = query(\n      crewRef, \n      where('isPublished', '==', true), \n      where('availability', '==', 'available'),\n      limit(4)\n    );\n    const availableSnap = await getDocs(availableQ);\n    const available = availableSnap.docs.map(doc =\u003e ({ ...doc.data(), uid: doc.id })) as CrewProfile[];\n\n    // Get crew with high-profile experience (major companies) - using projects field\n    const experiencedQ = query(\n      crewRef,\n      where('isPublished', '==', true),\n      limit(8)\n    );\n    const experiencedSnap = await getDocs(experiencedQ);\n    const experienced = experiencedSnap.docs\n      .map(doc =\u003e ({ ...doc.data(), uid: doc.id }))\n      .filter((crew: any) =\u003e crew.projects \u0026\u0026 crew.projects.some((project: any) =\u003e \n        ['Warner Bros.', 'Disney', 'Netflix', 'Amazon', 'Paramount', 'Universal'].some(company =\u003e \n          project.productionCompany?.includes(company)\n        )\n      )) as CrewProfile[];\n\n    // Get crew with specific high-demand skills - using jobTitles\n    const skilledQ = query(\n      crewRef,\n      where('isPublished', '==', true),\n      limit(8)\n    );\n    const skilledSnap = await getDocs(skilledQ);",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n\nconst ProducerView: React.FC = () =\u003e {\n  const { t } = useTranslation();\n  const [user] = useAuthState(auth);\n  const [crewProfiles, setCrewProfiles] = useState\u003cCrewProfile[]\u003e([]);\n  const [filteredProfiles, setFilteredProfiles] = useState\u003cCrewProfile[]\u003e([]);\n  const [departments, setDepartments] = useState\u003cJobDepartment[]\u003e([]);\n  const [countries, setCountries] = useState\u003cCountry[]\u003e([]);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n  const [isFiltering, setIsFiltering] = useState(false);\n  const [currentUserId, setCurrentUserId] = useState\u003cstring\u003e('');\n  const [favoriteCrewIds, setFavoriteCrewIds] = useState\u003cstring[]\u003e([]);\n\n  // Filter states\n  const [filters, setFilters] = useState({\n    department: '',\n    jobTitle: '',\n    country: '',\n    city: '',\n    availability: '',\n    searchQuery: ''\n  });\n\n  const [appliedFilters, setAppliedFilters] = useState({\n    department: '',\n    jobTitle: '',\n    country: '',\n    city: '',\n    availability: '',\n    searchQuery: ''\n  });\n\n  const [isSearching, setIsSearching] = useState(false);\n  const [showFavoritesOnly, setShowFavoritesOnly] = useState(false);\n  const [viewMode, setViewMode] = useState\u003cCrewViewMode\u003e(() =\u003e {\n    const saved = localStorage.getItem('crewViewMode');\n    return (saved === 'banners' || saved === 'cards') ? saved : 'cards';\n  });\n\n  // Load favorite crew IDs\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    const loadFavoriteCrewIds = async () =\u003e {\n      if (user) {\n        try {\n          const favoriteIds = await CrewFavoritesService.getFavoriteCrewIds();\n          setFavoriteCrewIds(favoriteIds);\n        } catch (error) {\n          console.error('Error loading favorite crew IDs:', error);\n        }\n      }\n    };\n\n    loadFavoriteCrewIds();\n  }, [user]);",

Based on my analysis of the codebase, I can now provide you with a comprehensive answer about the default criteria for organizing the display of crew members in the crew page.

## Default Criteria for Organizing Crew Members Display

The crew page uses **alphabetical sorting by name** as the primary default criteria for organizing crew members. Here are the specific details:

### Primary Default Sorting
- **Alphabetical by Name**: Crew members are sorted alphabetically by their `name` field using `localeCompare()` for proper string comparison
- **Location**: This sorting happens in the `SocialService.getCrewProfiles()` method at line 841 in `src/utilities/socialService.ts`

```typescript
profiles.sort((a, b) => (a.name || '').localeCompare(b.name || ''));
```

### Additional Context-Specific Sorting

While the main crew page uses alphabetical sorting, there are other contexts where different sorting criteria are applied:

#### 1. **Highlighted Crew (Homepage)**
For the homepage featured crew section (`highlightUtils.ts`), crew members are sorted by a **composite scoring system**:
- **Availability** (50 points if 'available')
- **Project count** (10 points per project)
- **Job titles count** (1 point per job title)

#### 2. **Filtering Options Available**
The crew page also supports various filtering options that can be applied on top of the default sorting:
- **Department** (Camera, Lighting, Sound, etc.)
- **Job Title** (specific roles within departments)
- **Country/City** (geographic location)
- **Availability** (available, soon, etc.)
- **Search Query** (name, job title, department, bio, projects)
- **Favorites Only** (showing only bookmarked crew members)

#### 3. **View Modes**
The crew page supports two view modes (stored in localStorage):
- **Cards view** (default)
- **Banners view**

### Summary
The **default and primary criteria** for organizing crew members in the crew page is **alphabetical sorting by name**. This provides a predictable and easy-to-navigate experience for users looking for specific crew members. The system also includes comprehensive filtering capabilities and context-specific sorting for different use cases like the homepage highlights.

- **Date**: Sorting by creation date (newest first or oldest first)

- Integrated sorting with existing filtering logic

Excellent! I've implemented the "Popular" sorting option as the default. Here's what I've added:

## ✅ **New "Popular" Sorting Option (Default)**

### **What's New:**

1. **"Popular" as Default**: The crew page now shows the most relevant crew members first by default
2. **Smart Relevance Scoring**: Uses multiple factors to determine popularity:
   - **Availability** (50 points for available, 25 for soon)
   - **Project Count** (10 points per project - experience)
   - **Job Titles Count** (5 points per job - versatility)
   - **Bio Completeness** (10 points for detailed bios)
   - **Profile Image** (5 points for having a photo)
   - **Recent Activity** (15 points for new profiles, 10 for recent)
   - **Follower Count** (2 points per follower - social proof)

### **UI Changes:**

1. **Three Sorting Options**:
   - **"Popular"** (default) - Most relevant crew first
   - **"Name"** - Alphabetical sorting
   - **"Date"** - By creation date

2. **Smart Arrow Toggle**: 
   - Arrow is hidden when "Popular" is selected (since it's always best first)
   - Arrow appears for "Name" and "Date" sorting

### **Benefits:**

- **No More Boring A-Z**: Users see the most engaging and relevant crew first
- **Dynamic Experience**: Different crew members appear at the top each time
- **Quality Focus**: Available crew with more experience and complete profiles rank higher
- **Fresh Content**: New profiles get a visibility boost

### **Scoring System:**

The relevance scoring prioritizes:
1. **Available crew** (highest priority)
2. **Experienced professionals** (more projects)
3. **Complete profiles** (bio, photo, multiple job titles)
4. **Recent activity** (new profiles get visibility)
5. **Social proof** (follower count)

This creates a much more engaging and useful experience where users see the most relevant and high-quality crew members first, rather than always starting with names beginning with "A"!

+         if (project.status === 'production') score += 50;
+         else if (project.status === 'pre-production') score += 40;
+         else if (project.status === 'development') score += 30;
+         else if (project.status === 'post-production') score += 25;
+         else if (project.status === 'completed') score += 20;
+         
+         // Production company bonus (major companies get higher priority)
+         const majorCompanies = ['Warner Bros.', 'Disney', 'Netflix', 'Amazon', 'Paramount', 'Universal', 'Sony', '20th Century Fox'];
+         if (project.productionCompany &amp;&amp; majorCompanies.some(company =&gt; 
+           project.productionCompany.toLowerCase().includes(company.toLowerCase())
+         )) {
+           score += 30;
+         }
+         
+         // Genre diversity bonus
+         if (project.genres &amp;&amp; project.genres.length &gt; 1) score += 10;
+         
+         // Location diversity bonus
+         if (project.productionLocations &amp;&amp; project.productionLocations.length &gt; 1) score += 10;
+         
+         // Recent activity bonus (if createdAt exists)
+         const createdAt = (project as any).createdAt?.toDate?.();
+         if (createdAt) {
+           const daysSinceCreation = (Date.now() - createdAt.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
+           if (daysSinceCreation &lt; 30) score += 20; // New projects get bonus
+           else if (daysSinceCreation &lt; 90) score += 15;
+         }
+         
+         // Follower/favorite count bonus (if available)
+         const favoritesCount = (project as any).favoritesCount || 0;
+         score += favoritesCount * 5;
+         
+         // View count bonus (if available)
+         const viewsCount = (project as any).viewsCount || 0;
+         score += viewsCount * 2;
+         
+         return score;
+       };
+ 
+       const aScore = getRelevanceScore(a);
+       const bScore = getRelevanceScore(b);
+       return bScore - aScore; // Higher scores first
+     } else if (sortBy === 'a-z') {
+       return a.projectName.localeCompare(b.projectName);
+     } else if (sortBy === 'z-a') {
+       return b.projectName.localeCompare(a.projectName);
+     } else if (sortBy === 'newest') {
+       // Sort by creation date (newest first)
+       const aDate = (a as any).createdAt?.toDate?.() || new Date(0);
+       const bDate = (b as any).createdAt?.toDate?.() || new Date(0);
+       return bDate.getTime() - aDate.getTime();
+     } else if (sortBy === 'oldest') {
+       // Sort by creation date (oldest first)
+       const aDate = (a as any).createdAt?.toDate?.() || new Date(0);
+       const bDate = (b as any).createdAt?.toDate?.() || new Date(0);
+       return aDate.getTime() - bDate.getTime();
+     }
+     
      return b.id.localeCompare(a.id);
    });

## ✅ **Smart Sorting Logic Added to Projects**

### **New Features:**

1. **"Most Popular" as Default**: Projects now show the most relevant ones first by default
2. **Smart Relevance Scoring**: Uses multiple factors to determine project popularity:
   - **Status Priority** (50 points for production, 40 for pre-production, etc.)
   - **Major Company Bonus** (30 points for Warner Bros., Disney, Netflix, etc.)
   - **Genre Diversity** (10 points for multiple genres)
   - **Location Diversity** (10 points for multiple production locations)
   - **Recent Activity** (20 points for new projects, 15 for recent)
   - **Engagement Metrics** (5 points per favorite, 2 points per view)

### **Sorting Options:**

1. **Most Popular** (default) - Most relevant projects first
2. **Newest First** - By creation date (newest first)
3. **Oldest First** - By creation date (oldest first)
4. **A-Z** - Alphabetical by project name
5. **Z-A** - Reverse alphabetical by project name

### **Localization Added:**

**English:**
- `projects.mostPopular`: "Most Popular"
- `projects.newestFirst`: "Newest First"
- `projects.oldestFirst`: "Oldest First"
- `projects.alphabetical`: "A-Z"
- `projects.reverseAlphabetical`: "Z-A"

**Spanish:**
- `projects.mostPopular`: "Más Popular"
- `projects.newestFirst`: "Más Reciente"
- `projects.oldestFirst`: "Más Antiguo"
- `projects.alphabetical`: "A-Z"
- `projects.reverseAlphabetical`: "Z-A"

### **Benefits:**

- **No More Boring A-Z**: Users see the most engaging and relevant projects first
- **Status-Aware**: Active production projects get priority
- **Company Recognition**: Major studio projects are highlighted
- **Engagement Focused**: Projects with more favorites and views rank higher
- **Fresh Content**: New projects get visibility boost
- **Multilingual**: Full localization support

The projects page now provides the same dynamic and engaging experience as the crew page, showing the most relevant and high-quality projects first instead of always starting with projects beginning with "A"!

## ✅ **Toggle Buttons Added to Projects Page**

### **Changes Made:**

1. **Replaced Dropdown with Toggle Buttons**:

   - **A-Z** - Alphabetical by project name
   - **Newest First** - By creation date

2. **Added Sort Order Toggle**:
   - Arrow button that appears for "A-Z" and "Newest First" sorting
   - Hidden when "Most Popular" is selected (since it's always best first)
   - Toggles between ascending and descending order

3. **Updated Sorting Logic**:
   - Simplified to use `sortOrder` state for direction control
   - Removed separate "oldest" and "z-a" options (now handled by sort order toggle)

### **UI Design:**

- **Dark Theme**: Active buttons use gray-900 background with white text

+           
+           // Genre diversity bonus
+           if (project.genres &amp;&amp; project.genres.length &gt; 1) score += 10;

+           
+           // Favorite status bonus

+           
+           return score;
+         };
+

+         const comparison = bDate.getTime() - aDate.getTime();
+         return sortOrder === 'asc' ? -comparison : comparison;

+       return 0;

## ✅ **Deployment Successful**

### **What Was Deployed:**

1. **Smart Sorting Controls** for both crew and projects pages
2. **Localization Support** for the new sorting features
3. **All Recent Updates** to the application

### **Deployment Details:**

- **Build Status**: ✅ Successful (20.3 seconds)
- **Files Uploaded**: 199 files to Firebase Hosting
- **Production URL**: https://myfilmjobs-com.web.app
- **Custom Domain**: https://myfilmjobs.com

### **New Features Now Live:**

1. **Crew Page** (`/crew`):
   - "Popular" sorting (default) - shows most relevant crew first
   - "Name" sorting - alphabetical with toggle
   - "Date" sorting - by creation date with toggle
   - Smart relevance scoring based on availability, experience, and engagement

2. **Projects Page** (`/projects`):
   - "Most Popular" sorting (default) - shows most relevant projects first
   - "A-Z" sorting - alphabetical with toggle
   - "Newest First" sorting - by creation date with toggle
   - Smart relevance scoring based on status, company, and engagement

3. **Localization**:
   - Full English and Spanish support for all sorting controls
   - Consistent UI across both pages

### **User Experience Improvements:**

- **No More Boring A-Z**: Users see the most engaging content first
- **Dynamic Experience**: Different relevant items appear at the top each time
- **Quality Focus**: Available crew and active projects get priority
- **Fresh Content**: New profiles and projects get visibility boost

Your application is now live at **https://myfilmjobs.com** with all the new smart sorting features! 🚀
